title: Ephemeral credit shadowing during fast failover causing temporary allowance mismatch
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Post-incident investigation found a transient mismatch between per-key allowance accounting and shard lease transitions during rapid failovers. Traffic spikes that coincided with shard eviction resulted in ephemeral "shadow" credits: credits that were briefly visible to the old shard and then re-applied (or lost) when the new lease reconciled state, yielding short windows of inconsistent enforcement (both silent over-allow and double-debit scenarios). This ticket captures the root cause analysis, proposed fixes, tests, and rollout plan to eliminate the race.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a per-key bucketed route with small window size (1s) and enabled burst credits for test key K-ALPHA
2) Simulate sustained high QPS from K-ALPHA until the shard is near max conn and a scheduled maintenance trigger initiates fast failover
3) During the shard handoff, concurrently replay the last 10ms of request stream to the new shard to mimic in-flight assignment duplication
4) Observe accounting logs and meter deltas: check for temporary allowance > allowed_quota OR negative residual on the new shard after reconcile
5) Verify the sequence numbers and lease tokens in the shard metadata and correlate with observed meter writes to identify duplicates or lost commits
hypothesis: The fast failover path performs a non-atomic snapshot + replay sequence: the old shard flushes pre-commit credits while the new shard applies replayed requests without a deterministic dedupe/tombstone marker. Under high concurrency, this leads to 'shadow' credits that either double-apply or are dropped depending on write ordering and transient network latency.
mitigation: 1) Short-term mitigation: increase conservative enforcement by enabling per-request idempotency checks for replayed request IDs (feature flag) and add circuit breaker to pause automatic replay if lease transfer times exceed threshold

2) Medium-term: introduce a lightweight lease-handoff protocol where the outgoing shard writes a 'handoff marker' with final checkpoint and sequence, and the incoming shard must reconcile using that marker atomically before applying replay
3) Long-term: replace non-atomic snapshot-replay with an atomic transfer or CRDT-inspired monotonic counter that guarantees at-most-once credit application across lease boundaries
acceptance_criteria: A1: Unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent failover + replay show zero cases of allowance > configured quota for a wide range of timings
A2: End-to-end canary for 5% of traffic with feature flag set shows no billing/metering divergence vs control after 48h
A3: Observability: add metric 'lease_handoff_reconcile_latency' and alert when reconciliation exceeds 200ms; dashboard shows stale-run rate <= 0.01%
A4: Post-deploy incident runbook updated and sign-off from SRE and Billing owners
rollout_plan: 1) Implement idempotency short-term mitigation behind ff/opt-in on a canary org
2) Run synthetic pressure tests and internal chaos (shard preemption) for 72h on canary cluster
3) Deploy lease-handoff marker protocol to staging and run interleaved load tests with production-like key distributions
4) Stage gradual rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated health checks and immediate rollback on alert
5) Post-rollout: run a billing reconciliation job comparing pre/post-meter deltas for top 100 customers for 7 days
notes: Investigation linked to customer-reported transient overages during last week's incident (INC-2026-031).
Observed anomalies mostly on routes with small time-window enforcement and aggressive burst policies.
SRE action: temporary FF enabled for high-risk tenants (flag: disable_replay_on_handoff)
testing_plan: Unit tests for handoff marker serialization/deserialization
Integration test that replays recorded production request sequences with injected latency and verifies at-most-once credit semantics
Chaos test that kills shard leader at random points and validates reconciliation correctness
Billing end-to-end: synthetic customer with deterministic request pattern to assert exact token counts
